transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-08-04 15:00 PDT
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Derek Liu (Redwood SE), Rachel Kim (EmberWave Head of ML), Tomás Rivera (EmberWave Platform), Priya Shah (EmberWave VP Product)

Summary:
Quick QBR-style workshop to align on uptime, unit economics, and next-phase pilot (Dedicated trial). Focus on benchmarks, SSO/SAML and KMS questions, and timeline for a canary rollout.

Topics covered:
- Recent usage trends and cost spikes in July
- Failure modes seen during weekend traffic surge
- Dedicated vs Hosted tradeoffs for EmberWave's SLAs
- Security/compliance: SOC 2, SSO, KMS, audit logs
- Roadmap map: pilot -> canary -> prod widescale
- Benchmark plan and golden prompt set

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood): hey everyone, thanks for making time, want to run through where we left off after the last sync and nail down pilot dates, i think we have about an hour, cool?
[00:18] Rachel (EmberWave): yep, got a hard stop at 4:10 but should be fine, Tomás and i wanted to start with the cost windows you flagged in your report, the spike on July 12th, that one.
[00:32] Derek (Redwood): right, so the spike looked like two factors, one was very long context sessions that bypassed our prefix caching and the other was a sudden burst of retries from a downstream aggregator, so end-to-end qps effectively doubled for a short window. we suggested shorter session TTLs for the KV cache and some client-side retry jitter.
[01:05] Tomás: yeah we saw a lot of KV cache misses — the warmup penalty is rough, we also have some older clients not honoring the cache-control headers.
[01:22] Maya: that's useful, for the Dedicated trial we'll show how warm pools + continuous batching reduce that cost. Derek can walk through the numbers.
[01:35] Derek: sure, quick mental model — with Dedicated you get reserved GPU pools. if your p95 target is 200 ms for short replies, Dedicated plus small continuous-batch windows keeps tokens per second high while preserving latency. quantization to int8 or int4 on the cheaper variants also drops token cost but we need to validate hallucination rates on your evals.
[02:10] Priya (EmberWave): can you remind me, what's the rollback if we see a quality regression after quant? how fast can we fallback to full-precision?
[02:24] Derek: immediate policy-based fallback; the serving runtime supports model variant routing so you can have canary quantized models and fallback to fp16 within a single request path. it's automated if quality monitors detect drift. sometimes the transcript or infra will call it, um, the fallback mesh — the logs show the switch.
[02:56] Rachel: ok that helps. on security, our compliance team asked specifically about SAML SSO, KMS integration for key rotation, and how audit logs are retained for 7 years, is that, um, supported?
[03:14] Maya: yes — SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning supported, KMS/HSM integrations for private deployments, and audit logs can be exported to your SIEM. retention beyond default windows is an add-on, we can include in the enterprise package.
[03:36] Tomás: is the Private deployment the same as VPC? we need air-gapped options for some customers later this year.
[03:45] Derek: two options: Private (customer VPC with Redwood control plane) or On-Prem (air-gapped package). Private gives near same UX, On-Prem is more of a lift. For this pilot, Private VPC should cover your needs, On-Prem can be scoped if required.
[04:12] Rachel: timeline question — if we start the Dedicated 72-hour trial mid-August, how long to provision?
[04:21] Maya: provisioning is typically 3–5 business days once we have the capacity request and PO for reserved trial capacity; for Dedicated trial we can compress it if you sign a short-form pilot agreement.
[04:35] Priya: what about SLAs — we need 99.9% uptime for inference endpoints and regional failover. can Redwood commit to that for Dedicated?
[04:47] Derek: Dedicated includes SLA-backed uptime higher than hosted default, and we have routing/fallbacks across regions to reduce single-region risk. we can show the exact SLA language in the contract.
[05:05] Tomás: i want to call out the weekend outage we had last quarter was due to an aggregator bug, but the cascade was because the model pool autoscale didn't add enough capacity in time — any knobs there?
[05:18] Derek: autoscale policies are fully configurable — min/max pools, scale step, and burst capacity. we also have predictive autoscale for steady diurnal patterns. for bursty aggregator cases we recommend a small buffer of reserved capacity plus burst policies.
[05:40] Rachel: okay, can we run a runbook simulation? like, can Redwood help simulate the aggregator burst to validate our autoscale and fallback?
[05:51] Maya: yes, that would be part of the benchmark plan Derek's preparing. we'll do a 72-hour stress window with synthetic traffic that mirrors your qps distribution.
[06:06] Derek: for the benchmark we'll need your golden prompt set (ideally 200 examples across short, medium, long contexts), the p95 target you want, and sample traffic histogram — Tomás said he'd share that.
[06:22] Tomás: i'll extract the telemetry exports and push to the shared folder after this call.
[06:28] Priya: about cost — the pricing model you proposed has an egress token credit and a reserved hourly pool cost, but we're concerned about token-level spikes for long-context sessions. any immediate mitigations?
[06:44] Derek: prefix caching + serialization of long contexts into shorter rolling windows reduces billable tokens. also reranking on the client side for low-value queries can avoid full decode calls. quantization helps too but again testing required for quality.
[07:05] Rachel: do you have any examples of customers who moved from hosted to Dedicated and saw 30% cost reduction?
[07:13] Maya: yes — one example (anonymized) in fintech moved time-series summarization to a Dedicated profile and used caching, dropping effective cost per thousand tokens by about 28% while meeting p95s. we can share the case study link.
[07:30] Tomás: i want the technical deep dive to include kernel selection details, because our infra team likes to understand where compilation differences come in — does Redwood expose kernel / compilation logs?
[07:45] Derek: we expose perf profiles and kernel-level metrics in the console; we'll prepare a short appendix for your infra team.
[08:05] Rachel: let's talk risk — what happens if there's a major model regression mid-pilot? we can't let customer-facing flows degrade.
[08:17] Derek: we recommend running pre-deployment evals plus live canary traffic at 1–5% of production, and auto-fallback to a previous model variant. we also can set up regression alerts tied to your golden prompts.
[08:35] Priya: on compliance paperwork, can you share SOC 2 report and PenTest summary before the contract?
[08:43] Maya: yes, we'll send SOC 2 Type II and the pen test executive summary once we have an NDA.
[08:55] Tomás: any vendor concerns about data residency in EU for some of our customers?
[09:02] Maya: we support regional endpoints and data residency controls, we can pin models and control logs location per account.
[09:12] Rachel: good. one more question — competitor sniffing: some RFPs mention Anthropic and Vertex as alternatives; how do you position Redwood on latency and observability?
[09:26] Maya: our position is production-first observability and cost controls — we instrument token-level traces and have first-class rollout tooling; in latency we optimize kernels and batching specifically for common seq-length distributions.
[09:43] Priya: ok, logistics — can you email the pilot agreement and a short checklist for data needed from our side?
[09:51] Maya: yes, will do.
[10:00] (discussion continues: Derek and Tomás dive into benchmark details, discuss exact traffic histograms, sample golden prompts, how to mask PII before sending to Redwood, how to configure audit exports)
[20:30] Derek: two technical notes — we recommend starting with a medium-sized model family (we called it earlier redwood-medium but naming in transcript is fuzzy) to validate throughput, then scale up to a larger variant if latency targets hold. also suggest enabling token-prefix caching and a small 200ms batching window for throughput-sensitive routes.
[31:05] Tomás: quick question about encryption at rest, is there granular key rotation per model or per account?
[31:15] Derek: we support per-account KMS keys; rotation policies can be delegated to your security team, integration with AWS KMS or customer HSM supported.
[41:10] Rachel: timeline recap and commitments?
[41:18] Maya: commitments: share pricing by 2026-08-06, Derek to share benchmark plan by 2026-08-09, Tomás to share telemetry and golden prompts by 2026-08-07; provisional start of Dedicated trial 2026-08-11 pending PO.
[41:40] Priya: that works, we'll try to expedite procurement.
[41:50] (brief chat about procurement path, PO templates and who on EmberWave legal will sign)
[50:00] Maya: ok, last items — do you want Redwood to run an initial canary with 5% traffic for two weeks post-trial?
[50:08] Rachel: yes, please. and include regression monitors tied to our golden prompt set.
[50:18] Derek: noted. we'll include canary plan in the benchmark doc.
[51:00] Maya: any blockers or open questions before we wrap?
[51:12] Tomás: just need the sales worksheet to model costs against our forecasting numbers.
[51:20] Maya: i'll send that today.
[51:30] Priya: thank you, everyone, this was useful.
[51:36] Maya: thanks all, we'll follow up with the docs and next steps.

Recap / Next steps (read back):
- Redwood: pricing worksheet, SOC2 + pen test exec summary, benchmark plan + canary plan (Maya / Derek)
- EmberWave: telemetry export, golden prompt set, procurement timeline (Tomás / Priya / Rachel)
- Target pilot provisioning: 2026-08-11 pending PO

Action items (repeat):
- Maya: email pilot agreement + pricing (due 2026-08-06)

End of transcript.
